title: Embed incident-derived safety checks into runtime release acceptance criteria
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket converts postmortem action items from the KV-cache coldstart incident (Jan 2026) into concrete release acceptance criteria and automated safety checks for runtime releases. The goal is to prevent regressions that could cause tail-latency spikes or extended cold-start periods by making incident mitigations a gating part of runtime-1.21 and subsequent releases.

Background:
- Postmortem identified three categories of root causes: (1) cache warming regressions during autoscale, (2) kernel scheduling mispredictions for long-context workloads, and (3) incomplete fallback routing when dedicated pools are saturated.
- Engineering implemented hotfixes (ENG-19872) and an initial autoscale warm-pool prototype (ENG-20411). Those changes need productized acceptance criteria, test coverage, and release-gates to be effective.

Goals:
- Define measurable acceptance criteria tied to the incident actions so runtime-1.21 cannot ship unless automated checks pass.
- Specify verification dashboards, synthetic tests, and rollout guardrails (canary metrics and automatic rollback triggers).
- Clarify scope and owners for test generation, infra changes, and console observability updates.

Scope (in-scope):
- Release gating criteria and automated checks for runtime kernel scheduling and caching behavior.
- Synthetic workload tests (cold-start and long-context) that run in CI and as pre-release canary verifications.
- Dashboard panels and alert rules for canary verification and post-release monitoring.

Out of scope:
- Large refactors of the kernel scheduler (covered by separate ENG epics).
- Non-runtime features (Console UX updates not required for gating, except dashboards specified below).

Requirements (high-level):
- A test harness in CI that runs the cold-start synthetic (detailed test plan in implementation notes) and fails a release if the 99.9th-percentile token latency increases > 2x relative to the baseline for the same commit range.
- Canary verification job that runs in the pre-release environment for at least 24h and asserts:
  * rolling 1-hour error rate < 0.1% on generation endpoints
  * 99th-percentile token latency within 1.5x baseline
  * KV-cache warm hit-rate >= 75% on warm-pool scale events
- Console dashboard with the following panels: tail-latency (p50/p90/p99/p999), kv-cache hit-rate, canary error rate, autoscale warm-pool fill duration.
- Runbook snippets and automatic rollback triggers defined for canary failure cases (thresholds above).

Acceptance criteria:
- (AC-1) CI synthetic cold-start test is implemented and added to the release pipeline; running it against an unchanged baseline commit produces pass/fail and historical trend for the last 10 runs.
- (AC-2) Canary job in pre-release runs for >=24 hours and produces a report; if any of the thresholds are breached the canary pipeline must block promotion and raise the configured alert.
- (AC-3) Dashboard panels and alert rules are created and documented in Confluence (link below). Alerts must route to on-call and SEV classification described in the runbook.
- (AC-4) Rollback automation is wired: a failing canary triggers a documented rollback play that stops release promotion and notifies stakeholders.
- (AC-5) Post-release smoke job runs for 72h to verify that KV-cache warm-pool behavior and scheduling metrics remain within threshold; metrics are ingested to the central observability workspace.

Implementation notes:
- Engineering will reuse the synthetic harness from ENG-17601 (long-context generator) and add a cold-start variant that deliberately scales down and recreates GPU workers to exercise warm-pool fill logic.
- Metric baselines will be derived from the 30-day window prior to the incident (Dec 2025). Workspace: https://observability.redwood.internal/dashboards/runtime-baselines (internal link).
- Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Incident+Safety+Gates (add new section 'Runtime-1.21 acceptance checks').
- GitHub PRs: PRs implementing tests and dashboards should reference this ticket and link back to ENG-19872 and ENG-20411.

Rollout & verification:
- Pre-release: Canary for 24h; slide to 72h on green. If canary fails, the release is paused and page on-call.
- Post-release: 72h verification job across regions. Any cross-region regression triggers incident-response runbook.

Dependencies:
- ENG-19872: hotfixes to cache warming (blocking for CI test to be meaningful).
- ENG-20411: warm-pool autoscale prototype (needed for production canary to be representative).

Open questions:
- What is the automated baseline extraction cadence for CI (daily vs weekly)? (owner: Jonah Kim)
- Should the KV-cache warm hit-rate threshold be adjustable per-model family? (suggested: yes; follow-up story required)

Deliverables:
- CI synthetic test and gating integration.
- Canary job with published run results.
- Console dashboard panels and alert rules.
- Runbook snippets and rollback automation playbooks.

Related artifacts:
- Confluence spec (see above)
- Observability dashboard (see above)
- ENG PRs: (placeholder) https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls?q=author%3Aeng-team+PM-78321
acceptance_criteria: CI cold-start synthetic test added to release pipeline and failing on >2x 99.9th-token-latency regression (relative to baseline)
Pre-release canary runs >=24h and blocks promotion on threshold breaches: rolling 1h error rate >=0.1% OR 99p token latency >1.5x baseline OR KV-cache warm hit-rate <75%
Dashboard panels and alert rules created and documented; alerts route to on-call with SEV mapping
Rollback automation stops promotion and notifies owners on canary failure
Post-release 72h smoke verification runs and metrics ingested into observability workspace
